FileDataIDs (or FileID) uniquely identify files in the Content Addressable Storage Container, and have been used as a replacement for internal file paths since Patch 7.0.3. For example, the "Interface/Icons/Temp.blp" texture can also be referred to using its [https://wow.tools/files/#search=interface%2Ficons%2Ftemp.blp 136235] FileDataID. Negative integers are temporary/local file IDs; these are not specified in the CASC root file and may change when the client is restarted.

Prior to patch 4.0.1, Fire Ward was a mage spell would cast a shield on the caster to absorb fire damage. However, unlike the gossip about Jaina Proudmoore's love for the orc Thrall, these rumors are likely true - though there is some doubt amongst certain scholars. In his youth, during military movements in Lordaeron, Proudmoore had several polite encounters with the high elf sorceress Kilnar Goldensword. Finster is as an intelligent mage. It takes him a little over an hour to finish preparations of his spells for a day. During this time he meditates, reads through spellbooks and other similar activities. He requires peace, quiet and comfort to allow for proper concentration. His surroundings need not be luxurious, but he requires they be free from overt distractions. He finds that exposure to inclement weather prevents his necessary concentration, as does any immediate injuries (although preparations go normally while he is healing from wounds from past battles). Once he was interrupted half way through his preparations and only finished half his spells.

Fire giants are a type of giant found in Northrend. As the name suggests, they are associated with fire and are recognizable by their smelting pot belt buckles, stovepipe helms, and dragonhide cloaks. Brann Bronzebeard claims that fire giants are creations of the titans. Since the corruption by Yogg-Saron, most known fire giants were servants of the Loken, with Ignis and Volkhan both directly created by the mad keeper. The fire giants were under the order of Loken to produce soldiers for the iron army. Following the defeat of Yogg-Saron and Loken, the Keepers brought back Ignis by their side to work in Ulduar's forges.

Fire Specialization is one of the passive specialization bonuses gained by a Mage when specializing into the Fire-tree at level 10. It simply increases the damage of the Mage's Fire-spells, which "ensures" that the Mage will be using Fire-spells instead of Arcane- and Frost-spells, thus making it an Fire-Mage.

In developing the fire arrow, dwarven tinkers took the expertise with gunpowder they gained developing rifles and rockets and turned it toward the bow and arrow. The fire arrow isn't itself an arrow. Instead, it's a small cylinder that attaches just below the arrow's head, with a short cord attaching the cylinder to a ring on the archer's quiver. When the arrow is fired, the cord ignites the charge inside the cylinder and propels the arrow incredible distances.

]] Fire and Iron is a short story by Matt Burns featured on the official site. It is the fourth in the Leaders of Azeroth series, released on April 16, 2011, and centers on the dwarves' Council of Three Hammers, with Kurdran Wildhammer as the main character. The story explains the cause of Sky'ree's death and the reason why Falstad replaced Kurdran as the Wildhammer representative on the council.
Fire hawks are large fiery bird-like creatures native to the Firelands. It takes them less than two days to fully grow. They exhibit much of the same behavior as birds on Azeroth.

Fire spiders are spiders found in the Firelands and rare locations in Pandaria. Despite being native to the Firelands, they aren't that much different from the spiders found on Azeroth, aside from being slightly more fire-oriented. They bite, they spin webs, they spit burning venom, and they capture their prey in cocoons of searing silk for later consumption. The fire spiders grow to huge sizes — the 12-foot-long ones in the Molten Front are actually the small ones. Fire spider venom is boiling hot, and the fluid they use to spin their webs is unbelievably viscous. Beth'tilac, the enormous matriarch of the Cinderweb brood, and her merciless offspring feed by sucking the magma and fire from t
Fire turtles are fiery turtles mostly found in the Firelands. A few notable ones have also been seen outside of the plane of fire and even being worshiped by pygmies on the Lost Isles.

A Fire Hawk Matriarch is an elite fire hawk at Molten Front in Firelands. She is aggroed when you take an egg for Peaked Interest. Formerly unreachable the Fire Hawk Matriarch will descend and then attack you. While killing her is not necessary for this quest, it can be difficult for some classes to get away/down quickly enough to outrun her.
Fire Hawk Eggs are laid by the fire hawks at the top of Fireplume Peak in the Molten Front.
Fire Scorpions are scorpions found in the Firelands, near the entrance. They are found in packs with a Greater Fire Scorpion.
Fire Blossoms are fire elementals summoned by Glubtok during the boss fight in the Deadmines.
Fire, Walk With Me is a player vs. player achievement earned for grabbing the flag and capturing it in under 75 seconds in Twin Peaks.

.]] Fire Camp Osul is home to the Osul tribe of yaungol. Found just southwest of the Ox Gate bordering Kun-Lai Summit, Jung Duk leads the Osul. Lin Silentstrike was captured back during Finish This! and can be found here as well. The Shado-Pan have claimed Longying Outpost, which is just to the southeast. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there. The totem Dominance, one of the objectives of the Pandaria exploration achievement The Song of the Yaungol, is found in the upper part of the mesa, not far from Battat and Urang. The Fire Camp Osul Digsite here actually covers Fire Camp Osul and Fire Camp Gai-Cho. It is a Mogu archaeology site.

Fire Camp Bataar can be found in the Yaungol Advance of south-central Kun-Lai Summit, in between Westwind Rest, Eastwind Rest, and the Chow Farmstead, just to the northeast of the great gate to the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. After two months, Garrosh retook the camp and made a Horde camp there. During the rise of N'Zoth, abandoned ale kegs were found here. They were recovered and delivered to Chen Stormstout.

Fire Camp Ordo can be found between the Kota Basecamp, Firebough Nook, and Westwind Rest in the northwestern reaches of the Yaungol Advance in south-central Kun-Lai Summit. The Ordo tribe of yaungol is led by the Ordo Warbringer who is protected by a shield cast by a blazecaster, embercaller, firespeaker, and a pyromancer. Once the fourth fire yaungol is dead, the warbringer's shield drops and can be attacked. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.

Fire Camp Ruqin is home to the Ruqin tribe of yaungol in east-central Kun-Lai Summit. Immediately to the north is the Grummle Bazaar and the eastern end of the Burlap Trail, just southwest is Mogujia, Muskpaw Ranch is to the southeast, and Fire Camp Yongqi is the closest settlement to the east. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.

Fire Camp Yongqi is the Yongqi tribe of yaungol settlement immediately to the south of the Temple of the White Tiger in eastern Kun-Lai Summit. What's left of Yinying Village is sandwiched between Yongqi and the temple, the Auburn Bluffs are to the east, and Lao & Son's Yakwash and Muskpaw Ranch are to the south. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.
Fire Elemental Remnants are fire elementals that spawn at the Blazing Strand in Darkshore during the quest Soothing the Elements in an attempt to disrupt the ritual.
Fire Elemental Ragers are fire revenants that spawns at the Blazing Strand in Darkshore during Soothing the Elements in an attempt to disrupt the ritual.

Fire Camp Gai-Cho is a heavily-defended yaungol fire camp in the northwestern reaches of Townlong Steppes, in the shadow of Kun-Lai Summit to the north, just downhill from Fire Camp Osul to the east, and overlooking the Gai-Cho Battlefield between the fire camp and Kri'vess to the south.
Fire Seeds are rarely found in Fire Leaf nodes in Borean Tundra.
__NOTOC__ Fire Spirit Salmon is created with Cooking (550); taught by trainers.
Fire Lotus Incense is provided as an objective for Instant Courage.
Finzy Watchwoozle is a goblin stable master located at the Hardwrench Hideaway in the Cape of Stranglethorn.

Fire Poppies are found all over the Ordon Sanctuary. They provide the standard Timeless Nutriment buff (+5% to all stats for 10 minutes), and additionally they "debuff" players with Smoldering Spores: "Healing 5% of maximum health every 3 sec."

The Fire-Watcher's Oath is an alternate version of the Censer of Eternal Agony that allows players to collect Bloody Coins. This item has the perk of being usable anywhere (including Battlegrounds), as well as not taking 90% of the player's health on use. It originally had an approximate 10% chance of granting a Bloody Coin and a long cooldown. It has since then been significantly buffed, to encourage players to obtain Bloody Coins from battlegrounds. For tactics and strategy, see the :Censer of Eternal Agony article.

Fire-Watcher is an exploration achievement earned for gathering 2,000 Bloody Coins obtained from world PvP on the Timeless Isle while transformed after using a Censer of Eternal Agony or a Fire-Watcher's Oath. Both are obtained from , the Emissary of Ordos, on the eastern edge of the Blazing Way. The achievement grants the title "Fire-Watcher".
Fire in the Yaung-hole! is a quest achievement earned for killing 15 or more Gai-Cho combatants with a single Highly Explosive Oil Barrel.
Firearrow Shoulderpads are a possible drop from Ordos, the world boss yaungol on the Timeless Isle.

Fire in the North: The Battle between Aegwynn and Sargeras is a book by Historian Llore which, as the name suggests, details the struggle between the Guardian Aegwynn and the Avatar of Sargeras in the wastes of Northrend.
